rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4-5, Figs 9-16: own LAI validation campaigns (Italy, Austria, Australia), own comparisons of metered vs suggested irrigation volumes, own user feedback. Q2: Section 5.1 and Figs 10-11: metered farm/district withdrawals compared with IRRISAT suggestions (farmers apply ~15% more); authors state adoption of IRRISAT produced an increase in irrigation efficiency through reduced volumes vs traditional practice; abstract: farmers schedule irrigation using the per-plot, near-real-time (24-48 h) advice; Section 5.2 Fig 13: standard FAO Kc would over-irrigate vs satellite-based Kc. Q4: Figs 9, 12, 15 validate the satellite LAI (the canopy variable driving ETcrop/CWR) against Licor field measurements; Fig 2 ETcrop vs eddy-covariance fluxes (corn, alfalfa, Sardinia 2010). Q5: Sections 5.1-5.3 report results separately for Campania (Italy), Marchfeld (Austria) and Bookpurnong (South Australia). Q6: Fig 11 district 'Boscariello' (1200 ha) measured vs suggested volumes; Table 2 service over 5500 ha/669 farmers; Section 5.2 scheme-level CWR for Marchfeld. Q7: Section 5.1: small farms (<10-12 ha) less efficient and reluctant to adopt the advice; absence of metering-based water pricing makes over-irrigation easier; farms above 10-12 ha more motivated to test volume reductions. Q8: Section 5.1: comparison of suggested vs actual volumes often difficult due to scarce field data; Section 5.2: missing information on crop management and soil conditions so interpretation is speculative; Section 5.3: comparison excludes above-average rainfall and further validation needed.
rows.notes: Q2 is a borderline yes: the water-saving effect is supported by metered-vs-suggested comparisons and water-managers' estimates of traditional volumes rather than a controlled before/after measurement of savings. Q3 no: user feedback is informal and about usefulness, not an independent measurement of water saving. Q9 no: Kc <U+00B1> SD (Fig 16) and CWR ranges (Fig 14) concern intermediate variables, not the water-use-efficiency result; the 15% figure and volume ranges carry no dispersion measure.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4-5, Figs 9-16: own field validation of satellite LAI, own satellite-based Kc and CWR estimates compared with applied volumes in three regions. Q2: Section 5.2 Fig 13: satellite-based Kc for two sugarbeet parcels lower than standard FAO Kc, authors conclude FAO Kc values would result in over-irrigation; Fig 14 satellite CWR vs supplied volumes; Section 5.1: IRRISAT CWR (3500-4500 m3/ha maize) below traditional volumes and reported reduction of water volumes; Fig 16 satellite citrus Kc vs FAO table. Q4: Figs 9, 12, 15 satellite LAI validated against Licor field LAI; Fig 2 ETcrop validated against eddy-covariance; Fig 13 satellite Kc curves as the intermediate step to CWR. Q5: Sections 5.1-5.3 report Kc/CWR results for Campania, Marchfeld and South Australian Murray-Darling separately. Q6: Fig 11 district-level (1200 ha) comparison; Table 2 four consortia 5500 ha; Section 5.2 irrigation-scheme-level CWR for Marchfeld. Q7: Section 5.1: effect depends on farmer adoption, which the authors found lower on small farms (<10-12 ha) and where water pricing lacks metering controls. Q8: Section 5.1 scarce field data for comparison; Section 5.2 lack of crop management and soil information; Section 5.3 further validation needed for tree crops and comparison excludes rainfall. Q9: Fig 16 reports citrus Kc from IRRIEYE as average <U+00B1> standard deviation; Fig 14 shows a range of CWR values (total vs effective precipitation).
rows.notes: Partial match: the study estimates ETcrop under standard (well-watered) conditions using actual canopy development, not actual (stressed) ET or Kcb act as named in the passage, and it reports no WPET; the supported part is RS-based Kc/ET improving irrigation management and limiting over-irrigation. Q3 no: a single method (satellite estimates vs applied volumes) per site; ground LAI checks validate inputs, not the water-saving result.

notes: Full text available. The paper is largely a system description with embedded own results (LAI validation, Kc/CWR vs applied volumes, user feedback); the ETcrop eddy-covariance validation (Fig 2) is presented here but attributed partly to D'Urso et al. 2010. Water-saving evidence is observational and partly based on water managers' estimates of traditional volumes.
